Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 97, verses 1–5:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿Indeed, We sent it down during the Night of Decree (1). And what can make you know what is the Night of Decree? (2) The Night of Decree is better than a thousand months (3). The angels and the Spirit descend therein by permission of their Lord for every matter (4). Peace it is until the emergence of dawn (5).﴾

Says the Exalted, may His remembrance be honoured: Indeed, We sent down this Qur'an all at once to the lowest heaven on the Night of al-Qadr, and it is the Night of Judgement in which Allah decrees the decree of the year. It is a verbal noun from their saying: "Allah decreed (qadara) this matter upon me," so He decrees (yaqduru) a decree (qadran).

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said in accordance with what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

◆ Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-A'la narrated to me, saying: Dawud narrated to us, from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The whole Qur'an was sent down at once on the Night of al-Qadr in Ramadan to the lowest heaven, and whenever Allah wished to bring about something on earth, He sent it down from it until it was complete.

◆ Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, saying: Dawud narrated to us, from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Allah sent down the Qur'an to the lowest heaven on the Night of al-Qadr, and whenever Allah wished to reveal something from it, He revealed it. This is His saying: ﴿Indeed, We sent it down during the Night of Decree﴾.

◆ He said: Ibn Abi 'Adi narrated to us, from Dawud, from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, and he mentioned something similar, and added to it: "And between its beginning and its end was twenty years."

◆ He said: 'Amr ibn 'Asim al-Kilabi narrated to us, saying: al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman al-Taymi narrated to us, saying: 'Imran Abu al-'Awwam narrated to us, saying: Dawud ibn Abi Hind narrated to us, from al-Sha'bi, that he said regarding Allah's saying: ﴿Indeed, We sent it down during the Night of Decree﴾: "The first of the Qur'an was sent down on the Night of al-Qadr."

◆ Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Husayn informed us, from Hakim ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Qur'an was sent down on a night from the highest heaven to the lowest heaven all at once, then it was separated over the years. Ibn 'Abbas recited this verse: ﴿So I swear by the positions of the stars﴾ and said: It was sent down in pieces.

◆ Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, from Dawud, from al-Sha'bi, regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, We sent it down during the Night of Decree﴾, he said: "It reached us that the Qur'an was sent down all at once to the lowest heaven."

◆ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, from Muslim, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: The Qur'an was sent down all at once, then our Lord sent down on the Night of Decree: ﴿therein every wise matter is made distinct﴾.

◆ He said: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿Indeed, We sent it down during the Night of Decree﴾, he said: The Qur'an was sent down all at once on the Night of al-Qadr, to the lowest heaven, and it was at the positions of the stars. Allah would send it down to His Messenger, some of it following after another. Then he recited: ﴿And those who disbelieve say, "Why was the Qur'an not sent down to him all at once?" Thus, that We may strengthen your heart thereby; and We have arranged it in gradual arrangement﴾.

The people of interpretation have said in accordance with what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

◆ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿the Night of Decree﴾: it is the Night of Judgement.

◆ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿Indeed, We sent it down during the Night of Decree﴾, he said: It is the Night of Judgement.

Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Muhammad ibn Suqah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: Permission is given to the pilgrims on the Night of al-Qadr, and they are written down by their names and their fathers' names, so none of them is left out, nothing is added to them, and nothing is taken from them.

◆ Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, saying: Rabi'ah ibn Kulthum narrated to us, saying: A man said to al-Hasan while I was listening: "Do you see the Night of al-Qadr in every Ramadan?" He said: "Yes, by Allah, other than whom there is no god, it is indeed in every Ramadan, and it is indeed the Night of al-Qadr, ﴿therein every wise matter is made distinct﴾. Therein Allah decrees every term, deed and provision, until its like."

◆ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Umar, who said: The Night of al-Qadr is in every Ramadan.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And what can make you know what is the Night of Decree?﴾

That is: And what informed you, O Muhammad, what the Night of al-Qadr is, which is better than a thousand months?

The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of that. Some of them said: The meaning of that is: Acting in the Night of al-Qadr in what pleases Allah is better than acting in other nights for a thousand months.

Mention of those who said that:

◆ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, who said: It reached me from Mujahid, regarding ﴿The Night of Decree is better than a thousand months﴾: its deed, its fasting and its standing in prayer are better than a thousand months.

◆ He said: al-Hakam ibn Bashir narrated to us, saying: 'Amr ibn Qays al-Mala'i narrated to us, regarding His saying: ﴿better than a thousand months﴾, he said: A deed performed in it is better than the deed of a thousand months.

Others said: The meaning of that is that the Night of al-Qadr is better than a thousand months, and in it there is no Night of al-Qadr.

Mention of those who said that:

◆ Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿better than a thousand months﴾: in it there is no Night of al-Qadr.

Others said regarding that:

◆ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam ibn Salm narrated to us, from al-Muthanna ibn al-Sabbah, from Mujahid, who said: There was among the Children of Israel a man who would stand in prayer through the night until morning, then strive against the enemy during the day until evening, and he did that for a thousand months. So Allah sent down this verse: ﴿The Night of Decree is better than a thousand months﴾: the standing in prayer on that night is better than the deed of that man.

Others said regarding that:

◆ Abu al-Khattab al-Jaroudi Suhayl narrated to me, saying: Salm ibn Qutaybah narrated to us, saying: al-Qasim ibn al-Fadl narrated to us, from 'Isa ibn Mazin, who said: I said to al-Hasan ibn 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him: "O blackener of the faces of the believers, you went to this man and gave him your allegiance," meaning Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan. He said: "Indeed the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was shown in his dream the Banu Umayyah climbing his pulpit one after another, and that grieved him, so Allah sent down: ﴿Indeed, We have given you al-Kawthar﴾ and ﴿Indeed, We sent it down during the Night of Decree. And what can make you know what is the Night of Decree? The Night of Decree is better than a thousand months﴾," meaning the kingship of the Banu Umayyah. Al-Qasim said: We counted the kingship of the Banu Umayyah, and it came to a thousand months.

The most similar of the sayings to the apparent sense of the revelation is the saying of the one who said: A deed in the Night of al-Qadr is better than the deed of a thousand months, in which there is no Night of al-Qadr. As for the other sayings, they are claims of false meanings, for which there is no indication from report or reason, nor are they found in the revelation.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿The angels and the Spirit descend therein by permission of their Lord for every matter﴾

The people of interpretation differed regarding the explanation of that. Some of them said: The meaning of that is: The angels descend, and Gabriel with them, and he is the Spirit, on the Night of al-Qadr, ﴿by permission of their Lord for every matter﴾, that is, by permission of their Lord, for every matter Allah decreed in that year, of provision, term and other things.

Mention of those who said that:

◆ Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿for every matter﴾: He said: What will happen in the year until its like is decreed in it.

Upon this saying, the report ends and the place of pause is at "for every matter."

Others said: ﴿The angels and the Spirit descend therein by permission of their Lord﴾: they do not meet a believing man or woman except that they greet them.

Mention of those who said that:

◆ It was related to me from Yahya ibn Ziyad al-Farra', who said: Abu Bakr ibn 'Ayyash narrated to me, from al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he used to recite: "min kulli imri' salam" (peace from every man). Whoever recited with this reading gave the meaning of "min kulli imri'" as "from every angel"; its meaning in his view was: The angels and the Spirit descend therein by permission of their Lord, from every angel who greets the believing men and women. I do not consider the recitation with it permissible, because of the consensus of the authoritative reciters against it, and because it contradicts what is in the codices of the Muslims; for in no codex of the Muslims is there a yā' in His saying "amr," and when it is recited as ﴿min kulli imri'﴾ a hamzah is attached, which in writing becomes a yā'.

The correct view in this matter is the first saying we mentioned before, according to what Qatadah interpreted.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Peace it is until the emergence of dawn﴾

The peace of the Night of al-Qadr from all evil, from its beginning until the rising of dawn of its night.

The people of interpretation have said in accordance with what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

◆ Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Peace it is﴾, he said: good, ﴿until the emergence of dawn﴾.

◆ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿from every matter peace﴾, i.e., it is all good until the emergence of dawn.

◆ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Jabir, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿Peace it is until the emergence of dawn﴾, he said: From every matter, peace.

◆ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding Allah's saying: ﴿Peace it is﴾: there is nothing in it; it is entirely good, ﴿until the emergence of dawn﴾.

Musa ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Masruqi narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Hamid al-Himmani narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from al-Minhal, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, regarding ﴿from every matter, peace it is﴾, he said: No matter occurs in it.

By His saying ﴿until the emergence of dawn﴾ is meant: until the emergence of dawn.

The readers differed regarding the recitation of His saying: ﴿until the emergence of dawn﴾. The majority of the readers of the cities, except Yahya ibn Wathab, al-A'mash and al-Kisa'i, read ﴿maṭla'i al-fajr﴾ with a fatha on the lam, meaning: until the rising of dawn; the Arabs say: "The sun rose (ṭalaʿat al-shams) rising (ṭulū'an) and emergence (maṭla'an)." Yahya ibn Wathab, al-A'mash and al-Kisa'i read it: ﴿ḥattā maṭliʿi al-fajr﴾ with a kasra on the lam, interpreting it as relying on the noun in place of the verbal noun, while intending that verbal noun.

The correct recitation in this matter, in our view, is the fatha on the lam, for its meaning is sound in the Arabic language; the maṭla' with a fatha is the rising, while the maṭli' with a kasra is the place from which one rises, and there is no sense of "the place from which one rises" in this context.

End of the commentary of Surah al-Qadr.

◆ Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, from Dawud, from al-Sha'bi, regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, We sent it down during the Night of Decree﴾, he said: "It reached us that the Qur'an was sent down all at once to the lowest heaven."

Mention of those who said that:

◆ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿the Night of Decree﴾: it is the Night of Judgement.

◆ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿Indeed, We sent it down during the Night of Decree﴾, he said: It is the Night of Judgement.

◆ Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, saying: Rabi'ah ibn Kulthum narrated to us, saying: A man said to al-Hasan while I was listening: "Do you see the Night of al-Qadr in every Ramadan?" He said: "Yes, by Allah, other than whom there is no god, it is indeed in every Ramadan, and it is indeed the Night of al-Qadr, ﴿therein every wise matter is made distinct﴾. ◆ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Umar, who said: The Night of al-Qadr is in every Ramadan.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And what can make you know what is the Night of Decree?﴾

That is: And what informed you, O Muhammad, what the Night of al-Qadr is, which is better than a thousand months?

The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of that. Some of them said: The meaning of that is: Acting in the Night of al-Qadr in what pleases Allah is better than acting in other nights for a thousand months.

Mention of those who said that:

◆ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, who said: It reached me from Mujahid, regarding ﴿The Night of Decree is better than a thousand months﴾: its deed, its fasting and its standing in prayer are better than a thousand months.

◆ He said: al-Hakam ibn Bashir narrated to us, saying: 'Amr ibn Qays al-Mala'i narrated to us, regarding His saying: ﴿better than a thousand months﴾, he said: A deed performed in it is better than the deed of a thousand months.

Others said: The meaning of that is that the Night of al-Qadr is better than a thousand months, and in it there is no Night of al-Qadr.

Mention of those who said that:

◆ Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿better than a thousand months﴾: in it there is no Night of al-Qadr.

Others said regarding that:

◆ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam ibn Salm narrated to us, from al-Muthanna ibn al-Sabbah, from Mujahid, who said: There was among the Children of Israel a man who would stand in prayer through the night until morning, then strive against the enemy during the day until evening, and he did that for a thousand months. So Allah sent down this verse: ﴿The Night of Decree is better than a thousand months﴾: the standing in prayer on that night is better than the deed of that man.

Others said regarding that:

◆ Abu al-Khattab al-Jaroudi Suhayl narrated to me, saying: Salm ibn Qutaybah narrated to us, saying: al-Qasim ibn al-Fadl narrated to us, from 'Isa ibn Mazin, who said: I said to al-Hasan ibn 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him: "O blackener of the faces of the believers, you went to this man and gave him your allegiance," meaning Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan. He said: "Indeed the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was shown in his dream the Banu Umayyah climbing his pulpit one after another, and that grieved him, so Allah sent down: ﴿Indeed, We have given you al-Kawthar﴾ and ﴿Indeed, We sent it down during the Night of Decree. And what can make you know what is the Night of Decree? The Night of Decree is better than a thousand months﴾," meaning the kingship of the Banu Umayyah. Al-Qasim said: We counted the kingship of the Banu Umayyah, and it came to a thousand months.

The most similar of the sayings to the apparent sense of the revelation is the saying of the one who said: A deed in the Night of al-Qadr is better than the deed of a thousand months, in which there is no Night of al-Qadr. As for the other sayings, they are claims of false meanings, for which there is no indication from report or reason, nor are they found in the revelation.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿The angels and the Spirit descend therein by permission of their Lord for every matter﴾

The people of interpretation differed regarding the explanation of that. Some of them said: The meaning of that is: The angels descend, and Gabriel with them, and he is the Spirit, on the Night of al-Qadr, ﴿by permission of their Lord for every matter﴾, that is, by permission of their Lord, for every matter Allah decreed in that year, of provision, term and other things.

Mention of those who said that:

◆ Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿for every matter﴾: He said: What will happen in the year until its like is decreed in it.

Upon this saying, the report ends and the place of pause is at "for every matter."

Others said: ﴿The angels and the Spirit descend therein by permission of their Lord﴾: they do not meet a believing man or woman except that they greet them.

Mention of those who said that:

◆ It was related to me from Yahya ibn Ziyad al-Farra', who said: Abu Bakr ibn 'Ayyash narrated to me, from al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he used to recite: "min kulli imri' salam" (peace from every man). Whoever recited with this reading gave the meaning of "min kulli imri'" as "from every angel"; its meaning in his view was: The angels and the Spirit descend therein by permission of their Lord, from every angel who greets the believing men and women. I do not consider the recitation with it permissible, because of the consensus of the authoritative reciters against it, and because it contradicts what is in the codices of the Muslims; for in no codex of the Muslims is there a yā' in His saying "amr," and when it is recited as ﴿min kulli imri'﴾ a hamzah is attached, which in writing becomes a yā'.

The correct view in this matter is the first saying we mentioned before, according to what Qatadah interpreted.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Peace it is until the emergence of dawn﴾

The peace of the Night of al-Qadr from all evil, from its beginning until the rising of dawn of its night.

The people of interpretation have said in accordance with what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

◆ Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Peace it is﴾, he said: good, ﴿until the emergence of dawn﴾.

◆ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿from every matter peace﴾, i.e., it is all good until the emergence of dawn.

◆ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Jabir, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿Peace it is until the emergence of dawn﴾, he said: From every matter, peace.

◆ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding Allah's saying: ﴿Peace it is﴾: there is nothing in it; it is entirely good, ﴿until the emergence of dawn﴾.

By His saying ﴿until the emergence of dawn﴾ is meant: until the emergence of dawn.

The readers differed regarding the recitation of His saying: ﴿until the emergence of dawn﴾. The majority of the readers of the cities, except Yahya ibn Wathab, al-A'mash and al-Kisa'i, read ﴿maṭla'i al-fajr﴾ with a fatha on the lam, meaning: until the rising of dawn; the Arabs say: "The sun rose (ṭalaʿat al-shams) rising (ṭulū'an) and emergence (maṭla'an)." The correct recitation in this matter, in our view, is the fatha on the lam, for its meaning is sound in the Arabic language; the maṭla' with a fatha is the rising, while the maṭli' with a kasra is the place from which one rises, and there is no sense of "the place from which one rises" in this context.

End of the commentary of Surah al-Qadr.

◆ Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Husayn informed us, from Hakim ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Qur'an was sent down on a night from the highest heaven to the lowest heaven all at once, then it was separated over the years. Ibn 'Abbas recited this verse: ﴿So I swear by the positions of the stars﴾ and said: It was sent down in pieces.

◆ Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, from Dawud, from al-Sha'bi, regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, We sent it down during the Night of Decree﴾, he said: "It reached us that the Qur'an was sent down all at once to the lowest heaven."

◆ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, from Muslim, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: The Qur'an was sent down all at once, then our Lord sent down on the Night of Decree: ﴿therein every wise matter is made distinct﴾.

◆ He said: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿Indeed, We sent it down during the Night of Decree﴾, he said: The Qur'an was sent down all at once on the Night of al-Qadr, to the lowest heaven, and it was at the positions of the stars. Allah would send it down to His Messenger, some of it following after another. Then he recited: ﴿And those who disbelieve say, "Why was the Qur'an not sent down to him all at once?" Thus, that We may strengthen your heart thereby; and We have arranged it in gradual arrangement﴾.

The people of interpretation have said in accordance with what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

◆ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿the Night of Decree﴾: it is the Night of Judgement.

◆ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿Indeed, We sent it down during the Night of Decree﴾, he said: It is the Night of Judgement.

Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Muhammad ibn Suqah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: Permission is given to the pilgrims on the Night of al-Qadr, and they are written down by their names and their fathers' names, so none of them is left out, nothing is added to them, and nothing is taken from them.

◆ Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, saying: Rabi'ah ibn Kulthum narrated to us, saying: A man said to al-Hasan while I was listening: "Do you see the Night of al-Qadr in every Ramadan?" He said: "Yes, by Allah, other than whom there is no god, it is indeed in every Ramadan, and it is indeed the Night of al-Qadr, ﴿therein every wise matter is made distinct﴾. Therein Allah decrees every term, deed and provision, until its like."

◆ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Umar, who said: The Night of al-Qadr is in every Ramadan.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And what can make you know what is the Night of Decree?﴾

That is: And what informed you, O Muhammad, what the Night of al-Qadr is, which is better than a thousand months?

The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of that. Some of them said: The meaning of that is: Acting in the Night of al-Qadr in what pleases Allah is better than acting in other nights for a thousand months.

Mention of those who said that:

◆ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, who said: It reached me from Mujahid, regarding ﴿The Night of Decree is better than a thousand months﴾: its deed, its fasting and its standing in prayer are better than a thousand months.

◆ He said: al-Hakam ibn Bashir narrated to us, saying: 'Amr ibn Qays al-Mala'i narrated to us, regarding His saying: ﴿better than a thousand months﴾, he said: A deed performed in it is better than the deed of a thousand months.

Others said: The meaning of that is that the Night of al-Qadr is better than a thousand months, and in it there is no Night of al-Qadr.

Mention of those who said that:

◆ Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿better than a thousand months﴾: in it there is no Night of al-Qadr.

Others said regarding that:

◆ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam ibn Salm narrated to us, from al-Muthanna ibn al-Sabbah, from Mujahid, who said: There was among the Children of Israel a man who would stand in prayer through the night until morning, then strive against the enemy during the day until evening, and he did that for a thousand months. So Allah sent down this verse: ﴿The Night of Decree is better than a thousand months﴾: the standing in prayer on that night is better than the deed of that man.

Others said regarding that:

◆ Abu al-Khattab al-Jaroudi Suhayl narrated to me, saying: Salm ibn Qutaybah narrated to us, saying: al-Qasim ibn al-Fadl narrated to us, from 'Isa ibn Mazin, who said: I said to al-Hasan ibn 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him: "O blackener of the faces of the believers, you went to this man and gave him your allegiance," meaning Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan. He said: "Indeed the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was shown in his dream the Banu Umayyah climbing his pulpit one after another, and that grieved him, so Allah sent down: ﴿Indeed, We have given you al-Kawthar﴾ and ﴿Indeed, We sent it down during the Night of Decree. And what can make you know what is the Night of Decree? The Night of Decree is better than a thousand months﴾," meaning the kingship of the Banu Umayyah. Al-Qasim said: We counted the kingship of the Banu Umayyah, and it came to a thousand months.

The most similar of the sayings to the apparent sense of the revelation is the saying of the one who said: A deed in the Night of al-Qadr is better than the deed of a thousand months, in which there is no Night of al-Qadr. As for the other sayings, they are claims of false meanings, for which there is no indication from report or reason, nor are they found in the revelation.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿The angels and the Spirit descend therein by permission of their Lord for every matter﴾

The people of interpretation differed regarding the explanation of that. Some of them said: The meaning of that is: The angels descend, and Gabriel with them, and he is the Spirit, on the Night of al-Qadr, ﴿by permission of their Lord for every matter﴾, that is, by permission of their Lord, for every matter Allah decreed in that year, of provision, term and other things.

Mention of those who said that:

◆ Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿for every matter﴾: He said: What will happen in the year until its like is decreed in it.

Upon this saying, the report ends and the place of pause is at "for every matter."

Others said: ﴿The angels and the Spirit descend therein by permission of their Lord﴾: they do not meet a believing man or woman except that they greet them.

Mention of those who said that:

◆ It was related to me from Yahya ibn Ziyad al-Farra', who said: Abu Bakr ibn 'Ayyash narrated to me, from al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he used to recite: "min kulli imri' salam" (peace from every man). Whoever recited with this reading gave the meaning of "min kulli imri'" as "from every angel"; its meaning in his view was: The angels and the Spirit descend therein by permission of their Lord, from every angel who greets the believing men and women. I do not consider the recitation with it permissible, because of the consensus of the authoritative reciters against it, and because it contradicts what is in the codices of the Muslims; for in no codex of the Muslims is there a yā' in His saying "amr," and when it is recited as ﴿min kulli imri'﴾ a hamzah is attached, which in writing becomes a yā'.

The correct view in this matter is the first saying we mentioned before, according to what Qatadah interpreted.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Peace it is until the emergence of dawn﴾

The peace of the Night of al-Qadr from all evil, from its beginning until the rising of dawn of its night.

The people of interpretation have said in accordance with what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

◆ Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Peace it is﴾, he said: good, ﴿until the emergence of dawn﴾.

◆ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿from every matter peace﴾, i.e., it is all good until the emergence of dawn.

◆ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Jabir, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿Peace it is until the emergence of dawn﴾, he said: From every matter, peace.

◆ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding Allah's saying: ﴿Peace it is﴾: there is nothing in it; it is entirely good, ﴿until the emergence of dawn﴾.

Musa ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Masruqi narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Hamid al-Himmani narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from al-Minhal, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, regarding ﴿from every matter, peace it is﴾, he said: No matter occurs in it.

By His saying ﴿until the emergence of dawn﴾ is meant: until the emergence of dawn.

The readers differed regarding the recitation of His saying: ﴿until the emergence of dawn﴾. The majority of the readers of the cities, except Yahya ibn Wathab, al-A'mash and al-Kisa'i, read ﴿maṭla'i al-fajr﴾ with a fatha on the lam, meaning: until the rising of dawn; the Arabs say: "The sun rose (ṭalaʿat al-shams) rising (ṭulū'an) and emergence (maṭla'an)." Yahya ibn Wathab, al-A'mash and al-Kisa'i read it: ﴿ḥattā maṭliʿi al-fajr﴾ with a kasra on the lam, interpreting it as relying on the noun in place of the verbal noun, while intending that verbal noun.

The correct recitation in this matter, in our view, is the fatha on the lam, for its meaning is sound in the Arabic language; the maṭla' with a fatha is the rising, while the maṭli' with a kasra is the place from which one rises, and there is no sense of "the place from which one rises" in this context.

End of the commentary of Surah al-Qadr.
